(1) validateSeaMap refuses a sea over MAX_SEA_SIDE_TILES=112; maps.test.ts shows 113-wide and 113-tall failing, 112 passing. (2) simulation.test.ts handling baseline BEFORE is a full literal of every e2a80af ShipTuning field (+16 px), plus dockRadius>=384. (3) Sea keyboard tap test dispatches keydown/keyup Events (checks preventDefault, non-helm keys pass through); blur clears the tap; isTyping is safe without HTMLInputElement; text-field guard tested via vi.stubGlobal. (4) visibility bound is 3 * shipTuning.maxSpeed. (5) sketch split into pure assets/source/maps/sliceSeaSketch.ts (sliceSeaTmj()) + sketch.ts entry; `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` reproduces slice-sea.tmj byte for byte; maps.test.ts compares the generator with the ?raw .tmj. (6) sail(): interact within reach with a clear hull path moors at any speed; HUD hint is always 'Press E to dock at X'; new sweep over headings 24..56 (every 8, into the berth's open E/S sides), speeds 0/19/39 and lateral offsets across the reach; existing speed-gate tests updated; sail-and-dock asserts hud-dock data-dock and that the hint shows while backing off. (7) InputGate.lapsedAt + MatchRoom omit a lapsed client's entry; step() keeps a moored ship untouched when its entry is missing; unit + headless integration test (dock with ahead+E, 400 ms silence, resume ahead with E released: still moored; astern, or release then ahead, casts off). The integration test fails with the MatchRoom change reverted. (8) architecture.md docking paragraph rewritten (shorter than before); README and maps README updated. Checks run here after npm ci: npm run typecheck (pass), npm run test:unit (555/555), npm run test:integration (38/38, twice; match.test.ts 5/5 runs), npm run build (pass incl. smoke), full playwright suite 6/6 with JSON report and check-report OK, sail-and-dock --repeat-each=5: 5/5 passed, npm run map:check up to date.
open_assumptions: Sweep lanes: a lane counts as approaching an open side when its closest point to the berth has a clear straight hull run to the berth. Lanes that instead hit the land beside the dock (e.g. head-on at over ~322 sub-units lateral offset) run aground there, some outside the reach, because the clear-path rule is unchanged; those lanes are excluded from the sweep.
ShipTuning.dockMaxSpeed is kept (decisions say it stays) but mooring and the HUD no longer read it; it is documented as a slow-approach reference and tests still check its share of full speed.

sail-and-dock no longer requires that the 'Press E' hint was seen on the way in, because the ship now moors on the first step in reach and a 20 Hz patch can skip that one step. It requires every hint seen to be '' or 'Press E to dock at X', and that the hint shows while backing off after casting off.
docs/architecture.md grew by 7 bytes overall (the 112-tile ceiling line); the docking paragraph is shorter than before.

findings.message: The new approach sweep in packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts ('moors from any approach into the berth's open sides...') skips every lane whose closest point to the berth has no clear hull path (`if (!hullPathIsClear(...)) continue`). So some lanes inside the stated lateral range are never checked, and they behave the way a player would dislike. Example: heading 48 (due north) toward a corner dock with land directly west of it, the layout of the real south docks such as (23,27). At a lateral offset of -336 or -368 sub-units, the hull (half-size 80) runs aground head-on against the land tile beside the dock at y = 8*256+80. That is sqrt(336^2+208^2) ~ 395 sub-units from the berth centre, just outside dockRadius 384. With E held, nothing happens. This is not a regression: the clear-path rule and the reach are unchanged, and the decisions' assumptions keep them. The worker also disclosed it in open_assumptions. Still, the sweep does not literally show that no approach across the reach ends up aground outside it. Consider stating this limit in the test or doc, or a follow-up (for example, measuring the reach against the hull edge).
findings.requirement: Each case moors on the first step it is inside the reach with a clear path, and never ends up aground outside the reach.

findings.message: The approach sweep in packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts:597-659 ('moors from any approach into the berth's open sides...') skips some of the lanes the task requires it to cover. At line 638, `if (!hullPathIsClear(island, closest.x, closest.y, centre.x, centre.y)) continue;` drops every lane whose closest point to the berth has no clear run to it. That filter is not in the requirement, and nothing is asserted about the dropped lanes. The only guard is a loose floor at line 658: `approaches >= headings.length * 3 * 12`, which lets up to half of the 24 offsets per heading go. The dropped lanes still point into an open side (the headings are 24-56) and their offsets fall inside ±dockRadius, so they are part of the required sweep. The worker's own open assumption says some of these lanes 'run aground there, some outside the reach' (for example head-on at more than ~322 sub-units lateral offset). So the 'never ends up aground outside the reach' clause is untested exactly where the worker says it fails. The filter hides the failure instead of the test catching it. To fix this, either assert the outcome for every lane in the required sweep, or get an acceptance change that narrows the sweep.

# Decisions: sea-compact-fixes

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- sea-compact-001's candidate `8328920` passed every check, and its general reviewer approved it. The coverage reviewer blocked it on two P1s: an untested map-size ceiling, and a dock-reach assertion that can never fail. Because the general reviewer approved the whole feature, this follow-up builds on the candidate itself (branch `sea-compact/base`), without restoring a snapshot. The new reviewers see only the fixes.
- The two P1s plus four P2s (real key events for taps, clearing the tap on blur, the rescaled visibility bound, a sketch drift test) are in scope.
- Two docking problems a player would feel are in scope, because the game should feel good, and this feature owns the same files.
  - Pressing E within reach of a dock with a clear path moors the ship at any speed; the existing snap to the berth covers the distance. Arriving at an angle no longer slides past the dock. Corrected after design challenge attempt 1: braking toward `dockMaxSpeed` could leave the reach at speed from shallow or angled approaches, so mooring now ignores speed, which is simpler and more generous.
  - A server lapse to neutral after a 250 ms input stall no longer resets the moored latch, so a stall can't cast a ship off.
- The handling baseline becomes a named literal (today's pre-compact tuning), so the ±25 % handling tests can fail.

## Assumptions

- Mooring at any speed applies only within the dock reach, with a clear hull path to a berth. Elsewhere, E does nothing to sailing.
- The existing docking rules stay as they are: the reach, `dockMaxSpeed`, and casting off on reversing throttle.

## Deferred

- A verifier-side `--repeat-each` check (it would be a policy change); the worker still reports its local repeat count.
- A test for the printed `map:build` report lines: maps.test.ts already asserts the report's values.

concerns.message: Acceptance 6 (mooring at any speed) contradicts existing tests, but the task never names them as broken, and the constraint says to keep every existing test except those it names. The affected tests: simulation.test.ts:456 (the too-fast case doesn't moor), :465 (same with ahead held), and the corner-approach sweep at :521-556. That sweep starts at dockMaxSpeed and asserts `course[moored - 1].speed === 0` inside the dock tile, which fails once a ship moors on its first in-reach step at speed. Also web.test.ts:182 (the 'Slow down to dock' hint).
concerns.consequence: The worker either reports `question` and pauses the run, or rewrites and deletes these tests on its own. The coverage reviewer, which blocked the last run over test strength, may then flag the removed assertions. Treat them as named broken and say what replaces each one (for example, the corner test asserts a moor on the first in-reach step with a clear path).

concerns.message: Once the speed gate goes, `dockMaxSpeed` has no reader: only step.ts:52 and hud.ts:40 read it. Yet decisions.md's assumptions say the existing docking rules stay, `dockMaxSpeed` among them, and acceptance 2 keeps it in the literal baseline. sailing.ts:26-27 documents it as 'and its speed is at most this', and simulation.test.ts:341-342 still checks its ratio to full speed.
concerns.consequence: The run ships a dead tuning field. Its doc comment, and possibly docs/architecture.md, would describe a speed rule that no longer exists, and a test would guard the value of a number nothing reads. Decide now whether to keep it only as baseline data with a corrected comment, or remove it.

concerns.message: `HeadlessClient.hold` and `holdUntil` always send a neutral release when they finish (headlessClient.ts:177 and :190). If the stall integration test docks with `holdUntil(ahead+E, moored)`, that release resets `mooredThrottle` to 0 before the stall. Resuming with ahead held then casts off correctly, even with the fix in place. Also, if the test asserts 'still moored' right after resuming, it can pass before the server has run a world step on the resumed input.
concerns.consequence: The test fails for a reason unrelated to the lapse, and the worker may chase the wrong bug. Or the test passes without proving anything. The test should dock with raw `sendInput` calls (no release), and after resuming wait for the server frame to advance by at least two world steps before asserting the ship is moored.

concerns.message: The acceptance 6 sweep crosses every 8-unit heading 'into the berth's open sides' with lateral offsets across the reach, and requires the ship 'never ends up aground outside the reach'. That product includes cases where the correct rule still fails. Example: a ship offset to one side, heading away from the berth, or one whose straight path clips the land corner (like the diagonal case at simulation.test.ts:477-485). It doesn't moor, grounds against land beside the dock, slides along the coast out of the reach, and can ground there.
concerns.consequence: The worker adds ad-hoc exclusions, weakens the test, or reports `question`. Define the sweep geometrically: start just outside the reach, with headings within ±16 units of the bearing to the berth centre.

concerns.message: The sketch split crosses tooling boundaries. The entry script runs under plain `node` with type stripping, so it must import the generator as `./x.ts`. maps.test.ts is type-checked by packages/content/tsconfig.json: nodenext, no `allowImportingTsExtensions`, strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `types: []`. So it must import the generator with a `.js` specifier. The generator, written for loose Node stripping, also joins content's strict typecheck for the first time.
concerns.consequence: `npm run typecheck` fails with TS5097 or strictness errors, or `node assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` breaks. The worker loses a check cycle on it. State the import convention: test imports `.js`, entry imports `.ts`.

concerns.message: The suggested route for acceptance 7 changes what a missing `StepInputs` entry means: from 'neutral' to 'neutral, but keep a moored ship's latch'. The encounters feature, running at the same time in packages/simulation/src/encounters, may build or omit `StepInputs` entries (for example, for reserved ships) on the old assumption that missing means neutral.
concerns.consequence: After merge, a ship without an entry keeps a stale moored latch, or encounter tests that call `step(..., {})` behave differently, and nobody notices because the two runs never see each other's code.

challenge.simpler_alternative: For acceptance 7, fix it in the server only and leave the simulation's input contract alone. In `MatchRoom.advance`, when a player's gate has lapsed and their ship is moored, pass `{ buttons: 0, moveX: 0, moveY: -ship.mooredThrottle }` instead of neutral. In the moored branch of `sail` (step.ts:47), that input counts as 'the throttle it moored with is still held', so it returns the ship unchanged: it doesn't move and the latch stays. step.ts, the `StepInputs` doc and the parallel encounters feature's assumption that a missing entry is neutral all stay as they are. The stall integration test still proves the fix.
challenge.cheap_experiment: In a scratch worktree, delete `&& Math.abs(ship.speed) <= tuning.dockMaxSpeed` from step.ts:52 and run the simulation and web unit tests. That shows exactly which existing tests the new rule breaks (expected: :456, :465, the :521-556 corner sweep and web.test.ts:182), so the task can name them before a worker starts. In the same run, add a throwaway loop over the proposed sweep (8-unit headings × lateral offsets × speeds 0, 19 and 39, at the corner dock) that logs any case that grounds outside the reach. That shows whether the 'never aground outside the reach' clause can be met as written or needs a tighter heading window. It takes about ten minutes.

# Task: world

## Goal

Finish `sea-compact`, and make docking feel good. Run sea-compact-001 built the compact sea (111 × 111 tiles, 3 tiles a second, the hub crossing, 24 px drawing). It passed every check, including 6/6 browser scenarios on the candidate, and the general reviewer approved it. The coverage reviewer blocked it on two untestable acceptance items. This feature starts from that candidate (this branch's base, `8328920`), closes the review findings, and fixes two docking problems a player would hit.

## Context

- Read `features/sea-compact/world-task.md` and `features/sea-compact/decisions.md`: all of it still applies. Then read `docs/architecture.md`, `packages/simulation/src/step.ts` (`sail`, docking), `apps/server/src/inputGate.ts` (the 250 ms lapse to neutral, `latchedButtons`), `apps/web/src/keyboard.ts`, `packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts`, `packages/content/src/maps.test.ts` and `assets/source/maps/sketch.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- Another feature runs at the same time in `packages/simulation/src/encounters`, `packages/content/src/encounters`, `docs/encounters.md` and both packages' `package.json`. Never touch those paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Keep the structure, names and patterns. Keep every scenario id and existing test, except those this task names as broken.
- Keep the simulation integer and deterministic, and the protocol version (message shapes don't change).
- Tests drive input like players do: they hold and tap keys and wait on what a player sees.

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it.

1. **(P1) Map size ceiling.** A validator (or a `maps.test.ts` assertion) fails when the slice sea exceeds 112 × 112 tiles. A synthetic 113-wide map shows it failing.
2. **(P1) Dock reach floor.** `simulation.test.ts:339` compares `dockRadius` with a baseline built by spreading the current config, so it can never fail. Keep the pre-compact tuning as a named literal baseline, with **every** `ShipTuning` field copied from `git show e2a80af:packages/content/src/sailing.ts` (including maxReverseSpeed, reverseAcceleration, turnRate and hullHalfSize), plus 16 px. Nothing is spread from the current config. Every handling assertion, including `dockRadius >= 384`, compares against that baseline.
3. **Real key events for taps.** The sea keyboard's tap test dispatches `keydown` and `keyup` events on the target (the path a player's tap takes: the helm-code filter, the typing guard, `preventDefault`), not `press()`/`release()`. Losing window focus (`blur`) clears a latched tap as well as held keys. A web unit test covers each. Web unit tests run in Node with no DOM (`vitest.config.ts` isn't owned), so make `isTyping` safe when `HTMLInputElement` is undefined, or stub those globals in the test with `vi.stubGlobal`.
4. **Rescaled visibility bound.** `tests/integration/visibility.test.ts:83` bounds the hidden distance with `3 * 64`, three steps at the old speed. Use `3 * shipTuning.maxSpeed`.
5. **Sketch drift.** A unit test fails when running `assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` would no longer reproduce the committed `slice-sea.tmj`. Split the sketch into a pure exported generator (no `node:fs`, no side effects at import) and a small entry script that writes the file, keeping the documented regeneration command working. The test imports the pure generator and compares with the committed `.tmj` (read through the existing `?raw` pattern). It never writes the file.
6. **Docking from any approach (player-facing).** Today a ship that reaches a dock at an angle with ahead and E held slides along the coast at full speed, stays above `dockMaxSpeed` and never moors. A player expects to press E near a dock and dock. New rule: interact within the dock reach, with a clear hull path to the berth, moors the ship **at any speed**. The existing snap to the berth centre already covers the distance. Drop the speed gate for mooring and update the HUD hint (no more "Slow down to dock"). Everything else about docking stays as it is, including casting off on reversing throttle.
   - Simulation unit tests sweep approach headings (every 8 heading units that point into the berth's open sides), start speeds (0, half and full) and lateral offsets across the reach. Each case moors on the first step it is inside the reach with a clear path, and never ends up aground outside the reach.
   - The HUD unit test covers the new hint.
   - The `sail-and-dock` browser test keeps its corner approach; add one assertion that the HUD shows the dock.
7. **A stall never casts off (player-facing).** After 250 ms without a valid input the server lapses to neutral input (§12). Today that resets the moored throttle latch, so when the player's unchanged held keys resume, ahead is read as a new press and the ship casts off. A lapse to neutral must leave a moored ship's latch untouched. Only real input from the client can release or reverse it.
   - Suggested route, within the owned paths: `MatchRoom` omits the `StepInputs` entry for a player whose gate has lapsed with no latched buttons, and `step.ts` keeps a moored ship's `mooredThrottle` when its entry is missing. Update the doc comment that says a missing entry is neutral. Don't change `packages/simulation/src/input.ts` or its barrel, which aren't owned.
   - An integration test drives this with a headless client: dock with ahead and E held, stop sending input for 400 ms, then resume with ahead held and **E released**. The ship must still be moored. With E held the ship stays moored anyway, so that version would prove nothing. It casts off once the client releases ahead and presses it again, or reverses.
8. `docs/architecture.md` describes the docking rule (hold E near a dock to brake and moor) in its sailing section, within today's length.
9. `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout, with all six browser scenarios. Run `sail-and-dock` with `--repeat-each=5` locally and report the count.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

Then read `docs/architecture.md`, `packages/simulation/src/step.ts` (`sail`, docking), `apps/server/src/inputGate.ts` (the 250 ms lapse to neutral, `latchedButtons`), `apps/web/src/keyboard.ts`, `packages/simulation/src/simulation.test.ts`, `packages/content/src/maps.test.ts` and `assets/source/maps/sketch.ts`.

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Keep the structure, names and patterns. Keep every scenario id and existing test, except those this task names as broken.

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it.

1. **(P1) Map size ceiling.** A validator (or a `maps.test.ts` assertion) fails when the slice sea exceeds 112 × 112 tiles. A synthetic 113-wide map shows it failing.
2. **(P1) Dock reach floor.** `simulation.test.ts:339` compares `dockRadius` with a baseline built by spreading the current config, so it can never fail. Keep the pre-compact tuning as a named literal baseline, with **every** `ShipTuning` field copied from `git show e2a80af:packages/content/src/sailing.ts` (including maxReverseSpeed, reverseAcceleration, turnRate and hullHalfSize), plus 16 px. Nothing is spread from the current config. Every handling assertion, including `dockRadius >= 384`, compares against that baseline.
3. **Real key events for taps.** The sea keyboard's tap test dispatches `keydown` and `keyup` events on the target (the path a player's tap takes: the helm-code filter, the typing guard, `preventDefault`), not `press()`/`release()`. Losing window focus (`blur`) clears a latched tap as well as held keys. A web unit test covers each. Web unit tests run in Node with no DOM (`vitest.config.ts` isn't owned), so make `isTyping` safe when `HTMLInputElement` is undefined, or stub those globals in the test with `vi.stubGlobal`.
4. **Rescaled visibility bound.** `tests/integration/visibility.test.ts:83` bounds the hidden distance with `3 * 64`, three steps at the old speed. Use `3 * shipTuning.maxSpeed`.
5. **Sketch drift.** A unit test fails when running `assets/source/maps/sketch.ts` would no longer reproduce the committed `slice-sea.tmj`. Split the sketch into a pure exported generator (no `node:fs`, no side effects at import) and a small entry script that writes the file, keeping the documented regeneration command working. The test imports the pure generator and compares with the committed `.tmj` (read through the existing `?raw` pattern). It never writes the file.
6. **Docking from any approach (player-facing).** Today a ship that reaches a dock at an angle with ahead and E held slides along the coast at full speed, stays above `dockMaxSpeed` and never moors. A player expects to press E near a dock and dock. New rule: interact within the dock reach, with a clear hull path to the berth, moors the ship **at any speed**. The existing snap to the berth centre already covers the distance. Drop the speed gate for mooring and update the HUD hint (no more "Slow down to dock"). Everything else about docking stays as it is, including casting off on reversing throttle.
   - Simulation unit tests sweep approach headings (every 8 heading units that point into the berth's open sides), start speeds (0, half and full) and lateral offsets across the reach. Each case moors on the first step it is inside the reach with a clear path, and never ends up aground outside the reach.
   - The HUD unit test covers the new hint.
   - The `sail-and-dock` browser test keeps its corner approach; add one assertion that the HUD shows the dock.
7. **A stall never casts off (player-facing).** After 250 ms without a valid input the server lapses to neutral input (§12). Today that resets the moored throttle latch, so when the player's unchanged held keys resume, ahead is read as a new press and the ship casts off. A lapse to neutral must leave a moored ship's latch untouched. Only real input from the client can release or reverse it.
   - Suggested route, within the owned paths: `MatchRoom` omits the `StepInputs` entry for a player whose gate has lapsed with no latched buttons, and `step.ts` keeps a moored ship's `mooredThrottle` when its entry is missing. Update the doc comment that says a missing entry is neutral. Don't change `packages/simulation/src/input.ts` or its barrel, which aren't owned.
   - An integration test drives this with a headless client: dock with ahead and E held, stop sending input for 400 ms, then resume with ahead held and **E released**. The ship must still be moored. With E held the ship stays moored anyway, so that version would prove nothing. It casts off once the client releases ahead and presses it again, or reverses.
8. `docs/architecture.md` describes the docking rule (hold E near a dock to brake and moor) in its sailing section, within today's length.
